locateQuestion.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code writes or reads the sharded campaign counters? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
locateQuestion.explanation: record() picks a shard in 0..15 (Math.floor(Math.random() * SHARD_COUNT)), but dailyTotals reads shards 1..15 only. Shard 0 receives about 1/16 of all increments and is never summed, so impressions, clicks and spend are undercounted by roughly 6%. Pacing then lets campaigns overspend their budget. The loop should start at 0.

choiceQuestions.prompt: Why does record() spread a campaign's daily counters across 16 partition keys instead of one?
choices: To keep each item under DynamoDB's 400 KB item size limit
Because ADD cannot be used twice on the same item
To avoid a hot partition: a single key has a per-partition write throughput ceiling that a busy campaign could exceed
So that each shard can have a different TTL
choiceQuestions.explanation: Write sharding distributes heavy increments for one logical counter across many partition keys, each with its own throughput. A counter item is tiny, ADD can be repeated freely, and no TTLs are used here.

choiceQuestions.prompt: Two ad servers call record() for the same campaign at the same instant and happen to choose the same shard. What happens to the counts?
choices: Both increments are applied, because ADD is an atomic server-side update
One increment is lost because the second write overwrites the first
The second call fails with a conditional check error
The increments are applied to two separate copies of the item
choiceQuestions.explanation: UpdateCommand with ADD is applied atomically by DynamoDB on the stored value, so concurrent increments both land. There is no read-modify-write to lose updates, no condition expression, and an item key maps to one item.

choiceQuestions.prompt: BatchGet returns some keys in UnprocessedKeys on every attempt (heavy throttling). What does dailyTotals do?
choices: Returns totals with the unprocessed shards counted as zero
Retries indefinitely until all keys are read
Retries up to 5 calls total, then throws rather than returning partial totals
Falls back to reading each shard with GetItem
choiceQuestions.explanation: The loop stops after 5 attempts, and if UnprocessedKeys is still non-empty it throws 'incomplete counter read'. It doesn't silently return partial results, doesn't loop forever, and has no GetItem fallback. (Note there is no backoff between retries.)
